title: Make-Break Codes
body:
The two codes a keyboard sends per keystroke:

- **Make** code: the key going *down*
- **Break** code: the key coming back *up*

Either one is a *scan* code $S$, where $0 \leq S \leq 127$. The break code is conventionally
the make code with the top bit set, which is why 127 is the limit: the eighth bit is the
up/down flag, not part of the key's identity.

You need both, not just make. Holding shift while pressing another key, auto-repeat, and
any game reading "is this key currently held" all depend on knowing when the key was
released, so the driver keeps a state table rather than a stream of characters.

Detected by a [[Scan Matrix]]; see [[IKBD Systems]].
